# Inside the Guāndì restoration: what the marks recover
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Guāndì** is what the evidence put back.

Guāndì's myth is history sanctified: the Records of the Three Kingdoms gave him a life, the Romance gave him a legend, and eight dynasties gave him a godhood. The Romance of the Three Kingdoms opens with the oath: in a peach garden, Guān Yǔ swore with Liú Bèi and Zhāng Fēi to die on the same day as brothers.  He kept it past reason — through capture, through Cáo Cāo's gold and titles, riding a thousand miles back to his sworn lord with the general's seal hung on his gate.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Guāndì
- **ASCII form:** guandi
- **Meaning:** ""Emperor Guan" — the deified general Guān Yǔ, god of war, loyalty, and righteousness"
- **Domain of influence:** War, Loyalty, Protection
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 關帝
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 89 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **關帝**. On the evidence, it means ""Emperor Guan" — the deified general Guān Yǔ, god of war, loyalty, and righteousness".

**Guāndì** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *guandi* and **Guāndì** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Guāndì** lives at [/sites/guandi/](/sites/guandi/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/guandi/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/guandi/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/guandi/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Guāndì** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Defense, Military & Security** — The god of war himself — loyalty as the armys oath.
- **Faith & Spiritual Organizations** — The deified general whose red-faced statue stood in more temples than any other figure in the Chinese world — loyalty worshipped.
- **Leadership, Governance & Public Administration** — The co-Sage of the empire; loyalty as governance.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Chinese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Tao Te Ching](/texts/tao-te-ching/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
